summary: George Turnour worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He served in the Ceylon Civil Service as Member of the Supreme Council in 1818 and Assistant to the Commissioner of Revenue in 1820.

George Uglow Pope was an Indologist and linguist. He founded and led Breeks Memorial School and Bishop Cotton Boys' School, taught at St Peter's School, and later served as Lecturer in Tamil at the University of Oxford (circa 1884–1908).

George V. Bobrinskoy was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Lutheran Theological Seminary at Philadelphia and Yale University under Franklin Edgerton. He spent his career at the University of Chicago, serving as Professor Emeritus of Sanskrit (1951–1967).

George Watt studied at Aberdeen Grammar School, the University of Aberdeen, and the University of Glasgow. He held positions at the University of Glasgow, Presidency University, the University of Calcutta, the Indian Museum, and the University of Edinburgh.

George de Roerich, a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Central Asian studies, studied at London, Harvard, the Sorbonne, and Paris under Sylvain Lévi and others. He directed the Urusvati Himalayan Research Institute and later worked at the Institute of Oriental Studies.

Linguist and Tibetologist George van Driem studied at the University of Virginia, Radboud University Nijmegen, and Leiden University. He held posts at Leiden University, served as Professor of Historical Linguistics at the University of Bern (2010–2022), and worked at IIT Guwahati.

Georges B. J. Dreyfus specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at traditional Tibetan monastic colleges and at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, later serving as Jackson Professor of Religion at Williams College.

Georges Dumézil was a scholar of linguistics, religious studies, and history who studied at the École Normale Supérieure under Antoine Meillet and Marcel Mauss. He held posts at Istanbul, Uppsala, and the EPHE, before holding a chair at the Collège de France.

Georges Perrot was an archaeologist and historian who studied at the École Normale Supérieure. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, the University of Paris, and served as director of the École Normale Supérieure (circa 1883–1904).

Linguist and Indologist Georges-Jean Pinault studied at ENS, Sorbonne Nouvelle, and EPHE, learning under Jean Haudry. He taught at Sorbonne Nouvelle and Blaise Pascal University before becoming a professor at the École Pratique des Hautes Études in 1999.

Georgios T. Halkias specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi and Oxford under Charles Ramble, held research posts at SOAS, Warburg, and Bochum, and became associate professor at The University of Hong Kong around 2012.

Gerald Hüther studied at Leipzig University. He worked at the Max Planck Institute for Experimental Medicine from 1979 to 1989 and held posts at the University of Göttingen and Universitätsmedizin Göttingen between circa 1995 and 2016.

Gerald James Larson was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Union Theological Seminary and Columbia University. He served as professor at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and as Rabindranath Tagore Professor at Indiana University beginning in 1995.
Gerardus van der Leeuw was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Leiden University from circa 1908 to 1916 and held a post at the University of Groningen from 1918 to 1950.

Gereon Kopf specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Temple University, conducted research at J. F. Oberlin and Nanzan universities, and served at Luther College and The University of Hong Kong.

Gergely Hidas specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his doctorate at Balliol College, Oxford, under Alexis Sanderson, and subsequently held posts as a Khyentse Fellow at Eötvös Loránd University and as a postdoctoral researcher at the British Museum.

Gerhard Oberhammer was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Innsbruck and the Sorbonne under Erich Frauwallner and V. Raghavan. After working at Utrecht University, he served as professor at the University of Vienna from 1964 to 1997.

Gerhard Wolf is a historian and archaeologist who studied at Heidelberg University. He held positions at Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1995–1998), Trier University (circa 1998–2003), and the Max Planck Society around 2003.
Gernot Böhme was a philosopher who studied at the University of Hamburg until 1965. He subsequently held a post at the Technical University of Darmstadt from circa 1977 to 2002.
Gerrit Jan Meulenbeld was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda. In 1978, he became an associate professor of Indology at the University of Groningen.
